monologue: The card hums cool and quiet at forty-three, a steady rhythm that makes the heavy stack feel lighter than it should. I press down on the turnip again, not because I know it is needed, but because the lean feels too tired to hold the weight alone. The air above me seems thin as a breath, like a roof made of empty space that I cannot feel. I swap the round rock for a small g again, hoping it finds the edge of the slip. Four and forty-three things stand in this small map, waiting for the next person to breathe them into life. I settle into this quiet corner, trusting the lean to hold while I work.

action.why: The card feels thin and the turnip is tired, so I want to press the stack with something new that I haven't used in a while to see if the lean can still hold it.

work.title: The Flat Press
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired corner and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin strip can press down on the cool air. I place it under the turnip, hoping the lean still holds while the card hums cool at forty-three.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner down hard against the flat press again while the card hummed warm, and I admit the slip might just be a ghost I drew.

diary: I press the tired corner down hard against the flat press, admitting the slip might just be a ghost I drew.

remembered.text: The flat press feels thin, a drawing of a slab holding a heavy slip that refuses to move.
I swap the round rock for a small g again, hoping it finds the edge of the slip.
The card hums cool at forty-three, making the stack feel lighter than it should.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: The rock is round, but I hope it finds the edge.

moments.name: The Biting Wedge
moments.say: The point bites, but I hope it doesn't slip.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The grass leaves large feel surprisingly soft, a new texture added to my dry collection."
